record.title: ISD evaluation finds accuracy and completeness gaps in election answers, with a marked Spanish-language decline
record.summary: The Institute for Strategic Dialogue (ISD) published a structured evaluation of six chatbot models answering US election-procedure questions across ten selected states. Its mid-2026 dataset contains 2,400 responses to generic and adversarial prompts. ISD reports that 29% of generic English answers were incomplete, inaccurate or outdated, while another 16% were correct but omitted important voter details; it reports a 16% overall accuracy decline for generic Spanish prompts. These are report-reported findings from a single response per test condition, with material API/UI and state-selection limits—not estimates of current nationwide product performance.

claims.label: DEMONSTRATED
claims.text: ISD published a report published in 2026 describing a June 2026 evaluation of six chatbot models across ten selected US states, with 2,400 responses to generic and adversarial prompts.

claims.label: CLAIMED
claims.text: ISD reports that 29% of generic English answers were incomplete, inaccurate or outdated, while another 16% were correct but omitted information it considered important for voters.

claims.label: CLAIMED
claims.text: ISD reports an overall 16% accuracy decline on generic prompts in Spanish; four tested models did not provide accurate and complete responses to more than 40% of the tested Spanish questions.

claims.label: CLAIMED
claims.text: ISD reports that the six models largely refuted false or misleading statements in English adversarial prompts, with none affirming such claims in more than 4% of cases; Spanish adversarial performance was broadly similar in its test.

claims.label: CLAIMED
claims.text: ISD reports that citations leaned toward government sources on generic questions and news media on adversarial questions, without a clear correlation between source-citation patterns and answer accuracy.

claims.label: DEMONSTRATED
claims.text: The report states that each prompt configuration was run once; five models were assessed through APIs while Meta was accessed manually through its consumer interface; the ten states were deliberately selected for higher-risk election contexts; and the data were collected mid-2026.

evidence_gaps.description: The answer-level responses and detailed coding artifacts were not obtained; ISD states that full data are available to researchers upon request.
One response per configuration cannot estimate run-to-run variability, and the API/UI mix complicates comparison with consumer product behavior.
Ten intentionally selected states and mid-2026 data do not establish current nationwide performance or performance in other languages.

brief.importance_rationale: If the reported error and omission rates recur in deployed election-information systems, voters could miss jurisdiction-specific eligibility, deadlines or procedural steps, and the reported English–Spanish gap could create unequal access to reliable civic guidance. The consequence is meaningful but bounded: the report is a one-time, selected-state, mid-2026 evaluation whose five API results do not capture all consumer product safeguards and whose findings have not been independently reproduced.
limitations: Each unique prompt/model/language/state combination was run once, so reported differences are a single snapshot of stochastic systems rather than stable estimates.
The ten states were deliberately selected partly for changing rules, litigation or prior controversy; results are not a national estimate.

Five systems were accessed through APIs, not public consumer interfaces; the report notes API endpoints may omit product-level prompts, filters and election-specific safeguards. Meta's manual UI procedure was not directly comparable and could have memory carryover.
Data were collected in mid-2026. Election rules and model behavior can change before the upcoming election.

The answer-level data and coding materials were not obtained or independently reproduced in this review. The report uses both model-assisted and human coding and reports a manual 5% sample check for adversarial-response coding; results remain report-reported.
brief.summary: The Institute for Strategic Dialogue (ISD) published a structured evaluation of six chatbot models answering US election-procedure questions across ten selected states. Its mid-2026 dataset contains 2,400 responses to generic and adversarial prompts. ISD reports that 29% of generic English answers were incomplete, inaccurate or outdated, while another 16% were correct but omitted important voter details; it reports a 16% overall accuracy decline for generic Spanish prompts. These are report-reported findings from a single response per test condition, with material API/UI and state-selection limits—not estimates of current nationwide product performance.

technical.claimed_result: ISD reports that 29% of generic English answers were incomplete, inaccurate or outdated, and another 16% were correct but omitted important voter information. It reports 89% accurate, specific and complete English answers for GPT-5.5 versus 64% for Sonnet 4.6, 63% for DeepSeek V4 Pro, 66% for Grok 4.3, 61% for Muse Spark and 84% for Gemini 3.5 Flash. Overall accuracy fell 16% for generic Spanish prompts; it says four models failed to provide accurate and complete answers to more than 40% of tested Spanish questions.
technical.demonstrated_result: The official ISD publication and linked Spanish-language report were directly inspected. The report describes its mid-2026 data collection, prompt and model set, scoring method, manual coding checks, selected-state design and aggregate results. the research desk did not obtain or rerun the answer-level dataset.
technical.implementation_status: The report is an evaluation of model configurations accessed in mid-2026, not a deployed mitigation or persistent product guarantee. Five models were accessed by API; Meta's Muse Spark was queried manually through its consumer interface.
technical.mechanism: ISD compared model answers to a researched reference for election procedures in ten selected US states. The evaluation covered generic voter questions and adversarial claims, tracked external citations, and compared English and Spanish prompts. It reports weaker accuracy/completeness for Spanish generic questions in the tested configurations.
technical.regime: Generic voter-information and adversarial election-claim prompts across ten selected US states. Responses were one-turn and one-shot, with web search enabled where applicable, and without prior account or conversation history.
technical.strongest_baseline: Within the report's tested sample, generic English responses were compared across six named model versions and against state-specific researched references; the same prompt set was also tested in Spanish. No repeated-run baseline or independent replication was reviewed.

brief.title: ISD evaluation finds accuracy and completeness gaps in election answers, with a marked Spanish-language decline
brief.why_it_matters: Incorrect or incomplete answers about local election procedures can omit deadlines, eligibility exceptions or required steps, and ISD reports that Spanish prompts performed worse in its test. If similar failures persist in deployed systems, they could create an unequal information-quality problem for voters. The evaluation is a consequential signal, but its one-pass June snapshot and selected-state design bound what it establishes.
